# Relay Relay moves jobs from a queue to workers. It retries a failed job five times with a longer wait each time, then parks it.
Why not a cron job? A cron job cannot see that a worker died. Relay does, and gives the job to another worker in under a second.
## Install ```sh npm install relay ``` ## Use Create a queue, then start a worker. Press Ctrl+C to stop it. The worker finishes its job first. ```ts import { createQueue } from "relay"; const queue = createQueue({ name: "mail", retries: 5, backoff: "exponential", maxWaitMs: 60_000, }); queue.add({ to: "team@example.com" }); ``` Check the queue from the shell: ```sh relay status mail relay parked mail --since 1h ``` The config file is JSON: ```json { "workers": 4, "park": true } ``` ![Architecture](docs/arch.png) See the [API notes](docs/api.md), the [install steps](#install) and the [changelog](https://example.com/changelog). The [retry guide](docs/retry.md) is new. - Jobs run at least once. - A parked job waits for a person, and the dashboard lists it. - Each retry waits twice as long as the one before.
